headline: 2 cops suspended after assault on cricketer Nayeem Hasan in Chattogram
summary: CMP Commissioner apologises as a three-member committee investigates the 'unprofessional conduct' of officers who allegedly beat the spinner with a pipe.
details: Two police personnel have been suspended following the alleged assault and harassment of Bangladesh national spinner Nayeem Hasan in Chattogram.
The suspended officers are Sub-Inspector Md Shafiqul Islam Bhuiyan of Khulshi Police Station and Constable Md Rasel Chowdhury.
The incident occurred in the Lalkhan Bazar area while Nayeem was returning home from Dhaka after playing a Dhaka Premier League match in Savar.

The Cricketers' Welfare Association of Bangladesh (CWAB) alleged that police displayed hostile behaviour, grabbed Nayeem by the throat, and beat him with a pipe despite being told he was a national cricketer.
CWAB further claimed that Nayeem was subjected to further mistreatment at the Khulshi Police Station before he could call for assistance.
CMP Commissioner Shawkat Ali visited Nayeem at his residence, expressed regret, and apologised for the unprofessional conduct of the officers.
A three-member investigation committee has been formed to probe the incident, and departmental proceedings have been initiated against the suspended officers.
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and several national cricketers have strongly condemned the incident, calling it 'unacceptable and inappropriate conduct'.

The Cricketers' Welfare Association of Bangladesh (CWAB) alleged that police displayed hostile behaviour, grabbed Nayeem by the throat, and beat him with a pipe despite being told he was a national cricketer.

CWAB further claimed that Nayeem was subjected to further mistreatment at the Khulshi Police Station before he could call for assistance.

CMP Commissioner Shawkat Ali visited Nayeem at his residence, expressed regret, and apologised for the unprofessional conduct of the officers.

A three-member investigation committee has been formed to probe the incident, and departmental proceedings have been initiated against the suspended officers.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and several national cricketers have strongly condemned the incident, calling it 'unacceptable and inappropriate conduct'.

headline: 5 units battling fire at Gazipur garment factory
summary: A blaze broke out at Matrix Styles Limited in the Digirchala area this morning, with flames spreading rapidly from the sixth floor.
details: A fire broke out at Matrix Styles Limited, a garment factory located near Malek's Bari in the Digirchala area of Gazipur, early this morning.
According to Md Azizul Haque, duty officer of the Bhogra Fire Service and Civil Defence Station, the blaze started around 10:05 am.
Five units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence are currently working to bring the fire under control, led by official Hiron Mia.
Eyewitnesses reported seeing thick black smoke and flames emerging from the sixth floor of the factory before the fire spread rapidly.
Workers and local residents initially attempted to douse the fire before alerting the fire service.
As of 11:45 am, the fire had not yet been brought under control, according to the duty officer.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage have not yet been determined.
caption:
A garment factory in Gazipur is currently engulfed in flames, with five fire units battling the blaze.

A fire broke out at Matrix Styles Limited, a garment factory located near Malek's Bari in the Digirchala area of Gazipur, early this morning.

According to Md Azizul Haque, duty officer of the Bhogra Fire Service and Civil Defence Station, the blaze started around 10:05 am.

Five units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence are currently working to bring the fire under control, led by official Hiron Mia.

Eyewitnesses reported seeing thick black smoke and flames emerging from the sixth floor of the factory before the fire spread rapidly.

Workers and local residents initially attempted to douse the fire before alerting the fire service.

As of 11:45 am, the fire had not yet been brought under control, according to the duty officer.

The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage have not yet been determined.
